NVDA.rationale: NVIDIA exhibits exceptional fundamental health and trajectory: Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY, +43% QoQ) with net income of $58.3B and EPS of $2.39 (+215% YoY), gross margins of 74.9%, operating margins of 65.6%, and net margins of 71.5%. The balance sheet is fortress-like with $195.5B equity, only $8.5B debt (D/E of 0.043), and $50.3B quarterly operating cash flow. The company dominates AI data center infrastructure with ~95% GPU market share and a sticky CUDA ecosystem. However, several factors temper the score below +0.5: (1) Valuation is no longer clearly cheap — at 29.8x trailing P/E it sits near the bottom of its 12-month range (29.4-66.8), but this reflects the massive Q1 earnings beat rather than a genuine discount; forward P/E of ~22x is reasonable but not a screaming bargain given the growth already embedded. (2) The stock has underperformed peers in H1 2026 (up only ~7% vs AMD +171%, Intel +278%), suggesting the market has already partially priced in concerns about AI capex sustainability, competition from custom chips (Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium), and tightening China export controls. (3) Customer concentration risk remains with 65% of revenue from four hyperscalers who are actively developing alternatives. (4) The $119B in supply commitments represent massive forward bets that could create inventory risk if demand softens. On the positive side, the Vera Rubin platform launch later in 2026, entry into the $200B data center CPU market, and Q2 guidance of $91B revenue provide credible near-term catalysts. The stock at ~$195 with forward P/E of ~22x appears fairly valued to slightly attractive for a company growing 80%+ with dominant market position.
